text:
Consider the general reaction given below at 400 K

$x\mathrm{A}(\mathrm{g})⇌y\mathrm{B}(\mathrm{g}).$

The values of $K_{p}$ and $K_{c}$ are studied under the same condition of temperature but variation in $x$ and $y$.

(i) $\mathrm{K}_{\mathrm{p}}=85.87$ and $\mathrm{K}_{\mathrm{c}}=2.586$ appropriate units

(ii) $\mathrm{K}_{\mathrm{p}}=0.862$ and $\mathrm{K}_{\mathrm{c}}=28.62$ appropriate units

The values of $x$ and $y$ in (i) and (ii) respectively are :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 23rd January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
For any gaseous reaction, the relationship between equilibrium constants is

$K_{p}=K_{c}(RT)^{\Delta n_{g}}$

where $\Delta n_{g}=$ (moles of gaseous products) $-$ (moles of gaseous reactants).

For the given reaction $x\mathrm{A}(g)⇌y\mathrm{B}(g),$ we have

$\Delta n_{g}=y-x.$

For reaction (i) : $\mathrm{K}_{\mathrm{p}}>\mathrm{K}_{\mathrm{C}}$

Since $K_{p}>K_{c}$, using $K_{p}=K_{c}(RT)^{\Delta n_{g}}$, $\Delta n_{g}$ must be positive. So the number of moles of gaseous products is more than that of reactants.

$\begin{array}{l} \Delta n_{g}>0 \\ y-x>0 \\ 85.87=2.586(0.0821\times 400)^{y-x} \end{array}$

Here $R=0.0821\mathrm{L}\mathrm{atm}\mathrm{mol}^{-1}\mathrm{K}^{-1}$ and $T=400\mathrm{K}$, so $RT=0.0821\times 400$.

From the equation

$85.87=2.586(0.0821\times 400)^{y-x},$

we get

Solving $\mathrm{y}-\mathrm{x}\simeq 1$

This means the products have one mole more than the reactants. So

$y-x=1\Rightarrow y=x+1.$

Taking the simplest whole numbers, we can choose $x=1$ and $y=2$ for case (i).

For reaction (ii) : $\mathrm{K}_{\mathrm{p}}<\mathrm{K}_{\mathrm{c}}$

Since $K_{p}<K_{c}$, using $K_{p}=K_{c}(RT)^{\Delta n_{g}}$, $\Delta n_{g}$ must be negative. So the number of moles of gaseous products is less than that of reactants.

$y-x<0.$

Using the same relation,

$K_{p}=K_{c}(RT)^{y-x},$

we write for reaction (ii)

$0.862=28.62(0.0821\times 400)^{y-x}$

Solving this, we find

$y-x\simeq -1$

So the reactants have one mole more than the products:

$y-x=-1\Rightarrow x=y+1.$

Taking the simplest whole numbers, we can choose $x=2$ and $y=1$ for case (ii).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2026 (Online) 23rd January Morning Shift

text:
In the given electrochemical cell, $\mathrm{Ag}(\mathrm{s})|\mathrm{AgCl}(\mathrm{s})|\mathrm{FeCl}_{2}(\mathrm{aq}),\mathrm{FeCl}_{3}(\mathrm{aq})|\mathrm{Pt}(\mathrm{s})$ at 298 K , the cell potential ( $\mathrm{E}_{\text{cell}}$ ) will increase when :

A. Concentration of $\mathrm{Fe}^{2+}$ is increased.

B. Concentration of $\mathrm{Fe}^{3+}$ is decreased.

C. Concentration of $\mathrm{Fe}^{2+}$ is decreased.

D. Concentration of $\mathrm{Fe}^{3+}$ is increased.

E. Concentration of $\mathrm{Cl}^{-}$is increased.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 23rd January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
In $\mathrm{Ag}(\mathrm{s})|\mathrm{AgCl}(\mathrm{s})|\mathrm{FeCl}{}_{2}(\mathrm{aq}),\mathrm{FeCl}{}_{3}(\mathrm{aq})|\mathrm{Pt}(\mathrm{s})$, the left electrode is the anode and the right electrode the cathode.

Anode: $\mathrm{Ag}(\mathrm{s})+\mathrm{Cl}{}^{-}(\mathrm{aq})\longrightarrow \mathrm{AgCl}(\mathrm{s})+\mathrm{e}{}^{-}$

Cathode: $\mathrm{Fe}{}^{3+}\qquad (\mathrm{aq})+\mathrm{e}{}^{-}\longrightarrow \mathrm{Fe}{}^{2+}(\mathrm{aq})$

Cell reaction, with $n=1$: $\mathrm{Ag}(\mathrm{s})+\mathrm{Cl}{}^{-}(\mathrm{aq})+\mathrm{Fe}{}^{3+}(\mathrm{aq})\longrightarrow \mathrm{AgCl}(\mathrm{s})+\mathrm{Fe}{}^{2+}(\mathrm{aq})$

$E_{\text{cell}}=E_{\text{cell}}^{\circ }-0.059\log \dfrac{[\mathrm{Fe}{}^{2+}]}{[\mathrm{Fe}{}^{3+}][\mathrm{Cl}{}^{-}]}$

$E_{\text{cell}}$ increases when this quotient decreases, that is, when $[\mathrm{Fe}{}^{2+}]$ is decreased (C), $[\mathrm{Fe}{}^{3+}]$ is increased (D) or $[\mathrm{Cl}{}^{-}]$ is increased (E). Statements A and B raise the quotient and lower $E_{\text{cell}}$.

Hence, the correct option is (A).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2026 (Online) 23rd January Morning Shift

text:
$\text{Match List - I with List - II.}$

  
    List - I
Functional group (detection)
    List - II
Change observed during detection
  

  
    A.
    Unsaturation (Baeyer's test)
    I.
    Red colour appears
  
  
    B.
    Alcoholic group (Ceric ammonium nitrate test)
    II.
    Silver mirror appears
  
  
    C.
    Aldehyde group (Tollen's reagent)
    III.
    Violet colour appears
  
  
    D.
    Phenolic group ( $\mathrm{FeCl}_{3}$ test)
    IV.
    Discharge of pink colour
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 23rd January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
For each functional group, recall the standard qualitative test observation (NCERT):

A. Unsaturation (Baeyer’s test)  

Baeyer’s reagent is cold, dilute alkaline $KMnO_{4}$ (pink/purple). With $C=C$ / $C\equiv C$, the pink colour gets discharged.  

So, A $\to$ IV.

B. Alcoholic group (Ceric ammonium nitrate test)  

Alcohols give red colour with ceric ammonium nitrate solution.  

So, B $\to$ I.

C. Aldehyde group (Tollen’s reagent)  

Aldehydes reduce Tollen’s reagent to metallic silver, giving a silver mirror.  

So, C $\to$ II.

D. Phenolic group ($FeCl_{3}$ test)  

Phenols give violet colour with neutral $FeCl_{3}$.  

So, D $\to$ III.

Hence the correct matching is:  

$A\text{-}IV,B\text{-}I,C\text{-}II,D\text{-}III$

Correct option: A
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2026 (Online) 23rd January Morning Shift

text: ' $x$ ' is the product which is obtained from propanenitrile and stannous chloride in the presence of hydrochloric acid followed by hydrolysis. ' $y$ ' is the product which is obtained from the but-2-ene by the ozonolysis followed by hydrolysis. From the following, which product is not obtained when one mole of ' $x$ ' and one mole of ' $y$ ' react with each other in the presence of alkali followed by heating?
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 23rd January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Stephen reduction of propanenitrile with $\mathrm{SnCl}{}_{2}/\mathrm{HCl}$ followed by hydrolysis gives propanal, so $x$ is $\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}\mathrm{CH}{}_{2}\mathrm{CHO}$.

Ozonolysis of but-2-ene, $\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}\mathrm{CH}=\mathrm{CHCH}{}_{3}$, cleaves the $\mathrm{C}=\mathrm{C}$ to give ethanal, so $y$ is $\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}\mathrm{CHO}$.

Both aldehydes have $α$-H, so with alkali and heat each acts as enolate donor and as acceptor, giving four aldol condensation products.

Ethanal with ethanal gives $\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}\mathrm{CH}=\mathrm{CHCHO}$ (but-2-enal), and propanal with propanal gives $\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}\mathrm{CH}{}_{2}\mathrm{CH}=\mathrm{C}(\mathrm{CH}{}_{3})\mathrm{CHO}$ (2-methylpent-2-enal).

The enolate of ethanal adding to propanal gives $\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}\mathrm{CH}{}_{2}\mathrm{CH}=\mathrm{CHCHO}$ (pent-2-enal), and the enolate of propanal adding to ethanal gives $\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}\mathrm{CH}=\mathrm{C}(\mathrm{CH}{}_{3})\mathrm{CHO}$ (2-methylbut-2-enal).


[IMG]

3-Methylbut-2-enal, $(\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}){}_{2}\mathrm{C}=\mathrm{CHCHO}$, would require the enolate of ethanal to add to propanone, which is not present, so it is not formed.

Hence, the correct option is (C).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2026 (Online) 23rd January Morning Shift

text: A cup of water at $5^{\circ }\mathrm{C}$ (system) is placed in a microwave oven and the oven is turned on for one minute during which the water begins to boil. Which of the following options is true?
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 23rd January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{O}(\ell )_{5^{\circ }\mathrm{C}}⟶\mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{O}(\ell )⇄_{100^{\circ }\mathrm{C}}\mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{O}(\mathrm{g})_{100^{\circ }\mathrm{C}}$

When water is heated in the microwave, its temperature increases from $5^{\circ }\mathrm{C}$ to $100^{\circ }\mathrm{C}$. After reaching $100^{\circ }\mathrm{C}$, it starts changing from liquid to vapour (boiling), so liquid water and water vapour can exist together.

During boiling, the water changes into steam and the volume increases (expansion).

Because of expansion, the system does work on the surroundings, so work done by the system is negative.

$\mathrm{w}=-\mathrm{ve}$

Since the microwave supplies energy to the water, heat is absorbed by the system, so $q$ is positive.

Also, water vapour has more internal energy than liquid water at the same temperature, so the internal energy of the system increases. Therefore, $\Delta \mathrm{U}$ is positive.

So, $q=+\mathrm{ve}$ and $\Delta \mathrm{U}=+\mathrm{ve}$.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2026 (Online) 23rd January Morning Shift

text:
Given,

(A) $\mathrm{n}=5,\mathrm{m}_{l}=-1$

(B) $\mathrm{n}=3,l=2,\mathrm{m}_{l}=-1,\mathrm{m}_{\mathrm{s}}=+\frac{1}{2}$

The maximum number of electron(s) in an atom that can have the quantum numbers as given in (A) and (B) respectively are :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 23rd January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
(A) $n=5$. So we look at all subshells for this value of $n$, i.e. $l=0,1,2,3,4$, and check where the given magnetic quantum number $m_{l}=-1$ is possible.

For $l=0m_{l}=0$, i.e. only one orbital is possible and it has $m_{l}=0$, so here we do not get any orbital with $m_{l}=-1$.

For $l=1m_{l}=-1,0,1\Rightarrow 2$ electrons can have $m_{l}=-1$ in this subshell, because there is exactly one orbital with $m_{l}=-1$, and one orbital can hold 2 electrons (with opposite spins).

For $l=2m_{l}=-2,-1,0,1,2\Rightarrow 2$ electrons can again have $m_{l}=-1$, because here also there is one orbital with $m_{l}=-1$, which can contain 2 electrons.

For $l=3m_{l}=-3,-2,-1,0,1,2,3\Rightarrow 2$ electrons can have $m_{l}=-1$ for the same reason: one orbital with this $m_{l}$ value, accommodating 2 electrons.

For $l=4m_{l}=-4,-3,-2,-1,0,1,2,3,4\Rightarrow 2$ electrons can have the given magnetic quantum number in this subshell as well (one such orbital $\Rightarrow$ 2 electrons).

Total number of electrons $=8$, because there are 4 such orbitals (for $l=1,2,3,4$), each holding 2 electrons.

(B) $n=3,l=2,m_{l}=-1,m_{s}=+1/2\Rightarrow$ only 1 electron is possible, because all four quantum numbers are completely specified. By Pauli’s exclusion principle, no two electrons in an atom can have the same set of four quantum numbers, so at most one electron can have this exact combination.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2026 (Online) 23rd January Morning Shift

text:
The correct statements from the following are :

A. Ionic radii of trivalent cations of group 13 elements decreases down the group.

B. Electronegativity of group 13 elements decreases down the group.

C. Among the group 13 elements, Boron has highest first ionisation enthalpy.

D. The trichloride and triiodide of group 13 elements are covalent in nature.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 23rd January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
(A) $\mathrm{B}^{+3}<\mathrm{Al}^{+3}<\mathrm{Ga}^{+3}<\mathrm{In}^{+3}<\mathrm{Tl}^{+3}$ : ionic size. This order means that the ionic radius increases as we go down the group (from $\mathrm{B}^{+3}$ to $\mathrm{Tl}^{+3}$). So the ionic radii do not decrease down the group. Therefore, statement (A) is incorrect.

(B) $\mathrm{B}>\mathrm{Tl}>\mathrm{In}>\mathrm{Ga}>\mathrm{Al}:\mathrm{EN}$. This is the actual order of electronegativity in group 13. It does not simply decrease from top to bottom; instead, there are irregular variations. So the statement that electronegativity decreases down the group is not correct. Therefore, statement (B) is incorrect.

(C) $\mathrm{B}>\mathrm{Tl}>\mathrm{Ga}>\mathrm{Al}>\mathrm{In}:$ IE. From this order of first ionisation enthalpy, we can see that boron has the highest first ionisation enthalpy among the group 13 elements. So statement (C) is correct.

(D) Trichlorides and triiodides of group $13^{\text{th}}$ elements are covalent in nature. The $\mathrm{MCl}_{3}$ and $\mathrm{MI}_{3}$ (where M is a group 13 element) have high polarising power due to the small, highly charged $\mathrm{M}^{3+}$ ion, so they form covalent bonds with halide ions. Hence, statement (D) is also correct.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2026 (Online) 23rd January Morning Shift

text: Identify the molecule $(X)$ with maximum number of lone pairs of electrons (obtained using Lewis dot structure) among $\mathrm{HNO}_{3},\mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{SO}_{4},\mathrm{NF}_{3}$ and $\mathrm{O}_{3}$. Choose the correct bond angle made by the central atom of the molecule $(X)$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 23rd January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Counting all lone pairs in each Lewis structure:

$\mathrm{HNO}{}_{3}$: the O–H oxygen has 2, the N=O oxygen has 2 and the N–O${}^{-}$ oxygen has 3, a total of 7.

$\mathrm{H}{}_{2}\mathrm{SO}{}_{4}$: the two O–H oxygens have 2 each and the two S=O oxygens have 2 each, a total of 8.

$\mathrm{NF}{}_{3}$: N has 1 and each F has 3, a total of $1+3\times 3=10$.

$\mathrm{O}{}_{3}$: the central O has 1, the terminal =O has 2 and the terminal O${}^{-}$ has 3, a total of 6.

So X is $\mathrm{NF}{}_{3}$.


[IMG]

N in $\mathrm{NF}{}_{3}$ has three bond pairs and one lone pair ($\mathrm{sp}^{3}$, pyramidal). The highly electronegative F atoms draw the bonding pairs away from N, so bond pair–bond pair repulsion is weaker than in $\mathrm{NH}{}_{3}$ ($107^{\circ }$) and the F–N–F bond angle is about $102^{\circ }$.

Hence, the correct option is (B).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2026 (Online) 23rd January Morning Shift

text:
From the given following (A to D) cyclic structures, those which will not react with Tollen's reagent are:


[IMG]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 23rd January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Tollens' reagent is reduced only by a free aldehyde group, which a cyclic sugar can supply only when its anomeric carbon (the ring carbon bonded to the ring oxygen) carries a free $-\mathrm{OH}$ group, i.e. it is a hemiacetal that can open to the $-\mathrm{CHO}$ form.

In structures A and D the anomeric carbon carries $-\mathrm{OH}$; they are hemiacetals, open to the aldehyde form and react with Tollens' reagent.

In structures B and C the anomeric carbon carries $-\mathrm{OCH}{}_{3}$; they are methyl glycosides (acetals), the ring cannot open in the alkaline reagent and no $-\mathrm{CHO}$ group is formed, so they do not react.

Hence, the correct option is (D).

text:
Given below are two statements :

Statement I : Sublimation is used for the separation and purification of compounds with low melting point.

Statement II : The boiling point of a liquid increases as the external pressure is reduced. In the light of the above statements, 

choose the correct answer from the options given below :
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 23rd January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Statement I: False. Sublimation is used to separate/purify sublimable (volatile) solids—solids that pass directly from solid to vapour on heating. This depends on having sufficient vapour pressure in the solid state, not simply on having a low melting point.

Statement II: False. The boiling point decreases when external pressure is reduced (principle of vacuum distillation).

✅ Correct option: A (Both Statement I and Statement II are false).

text:
Consider the following compounds :


[IMG]


Arrange these compounds in the increasing order of reactivity with nitrating mixture.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 23rd January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Nitration is an electrophilic substitution, so its rate rises with the electron density of the benzene ring.

In c ($\mathrm{C}{}_{6}\mathrm{H}{}_{5}\mathrm{OCH}{}_{3}$), the $+R$ effect of $-\mathrm{OCH}{}_{3}$ outweighs its $-I$ effect, so the ring is activated and reacts fastest.

In a ($\mathrm{C}{}_{6}\mathrm{H}{}_{5}\mathrm{Cl}$), the $-I$ effect of Cl outweighs its $+R$ effect, so the ring is weakly deactivated.

In b ($\mathrm{C}{}_{6}\mathrm{H}{}_{5}\mathrm{NO}{}_{2}$), $-\mathrm{NO}{}_{2}$ withdraws electrons by both $-I$ and $-R$ effects, so the ring is strongly deactivated and reacts slowest.

Increasing order of reactivity towards the nitrating mixture: $\mathrm{b}<\mathrm{a}<\mathrm{c}$.

Hence, the correct option is (D).

text:
The statements that are incorrect about the nickel(II) complex of dimethylglyoxime are :

A. It is red in colour.

B. It has a high solubility in water at $\mathrm{pH}=9$.

C. The Ni ion has two unpaired d-electrons.

D. The $\mathrm{N}-\mathrm{Ni}-\mathrm{N}$ bond angle is almost close to $90^{\circ }$.

E. The complex contains four five-membered metallacycles (metal containing rings).

Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 23rd January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
In bis(dimethylglyoximato)nickel(II), $\mathrm{Ni}{}^{2+}$ ($3d^{8}$) is bound to the four N atoms of two dimethylglyoximate ions in a square planar $\mathrm{dsp}^{2}$ arrangement.


[IMG]

A is correct: the complex is a rosy red precipitate.

B is incorrect: the complex is precipitated from weakly ammoniacal solution (pH about 9) because it is insoluble in water.

C is incorrect: in the square planar $\mathrm{dsp}^{2}$ complex all eight d electrons are paired, so it is diamagnetic.

D is correct: adjacent N–Ni–N bond angles in a square planar complex are close to $90^{\circ }$.

E is incorrect: each dimethylglyoximate forms one five-membered chelate ring (Ni–N=C–C=N), so there are only two five-membered metallacycles; the other two rings, closed by O–H···O hydrogen bonds, are six-membered.

The incorrect statements are B, C and E.

Hence, the correct option is (C).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2026 (Online) 23rd January Morning Shift

text:
Given below are two statements :

Statement I : $[\mathrm{CoBr}_{4}]^{2-}$ ion will absorb light of lower energy than $[\mathrm{CoCl}_{4}]^{2-}$ ion.

Statement II : In $[\mathrm{CoI}_{4}]^{2-}$ ion, the energy separation between the two set of d-orbitals is more than $[\mathrm{CoCl}_{4}]^{2-}$ ion.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below :
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 23rd January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
In the spectrochemical series the field strength of the halide ligands is $\mathrm{I}{}^{-}<\mathrm{Br}{}^{-}<\mathrm{Cl}{}^{-}$, so the tetrahedral splitting $\Delta _{t}$ of the $[\mathrm{CoX}{}_{4}]{}^{2-}$ ions follows the same order.

$\Delta _{t}$ of $[\mathrm{CoBr}{}_{4}]{}^{2-}$ is smaller than that of $[\mathrm{CoCl}{}_{4}]{}^{2-}$, so $[\mathrm{CoBr}{}_{4}]{}^{2-}$ absorbs light of lower energy: Statement I is true.

$\Delta _{t}$ of $[\mathrm{CoI}{}_{4}]{}^{2-}$ is smaller, not larger, than that of $[\mathrm{CoCl}{}_{4}]{}^{2-}$: Statement II is false.

Hence, the correct option is (D).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2026 (Online) 23rd January Morning Shift

text: Which of the following statements regarding the energy of the stationary state is true in the following one - electron systems ?
options: $-1.09\times 10^{-18}\mathrm{J}$ for second orbit of H atom.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 23rd January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
For one–electron (hydrogen-like) systems, the energy of the $n^{\text{th}}$ stationary state is (NCERT):

$E_{n}=-2.18\times 10^{-18}\frac{Z^{2}}{n^{2}}\text{J}$

where $Z$ is the atomic number and $n$ is the orbit number.

Check each option
Option A: Second orbit of $\mathrm{He}^{+}$  

Here $Z=2,n=2$

$E_{2}=-2.18\times 10^{-18}\frac{2^{2}}{2^{2}}=-2.18\times 10^{-18}\text{J}$

Given is $+2.18\times 10^{-18}$ J (positive), so false.

Option B: First orbit of $\mathrm{He}^{+}$  

$Z=2,n=1$

$E_{1}=-2.18\times 10^{-18}\frac{4}{1}=-8.72\times 10^{-18}\text{J}$

Given is $+8.72\times 10^{-18}$ J, so false.

Option C: Second orbit of H atom  

$Z=1,n=2$

$E_{2}=-2.18\times 10^{-18}\frac{1}{4}=-0.545\times 10^{-18}\text{J}$

Given is $-1.09\times 10^{-18}$ J, so false.

Option D: Third orbit of $\mathrm{Li}^{2+}$  

$Z=3,n=3$

$E_{3}=-2.18\times 10^{-18}\frac{9}{9}=-2.18\times 10^{-18}\text{J}$

This matches the given value, so true.

Correct option: D

text: The crystal field splitting energy of $[\mathrm{Co}(\text{oxalate})_{3}]^{3-}$ complex is ' $n^{'}$ times that of the $[\mathrm{Cr}(\text{oxalate})_{3}]^{3-}$ complex. Here ' $n$ ' is $____$ . (Assume $\Delta _{0}\gg P$ )
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 23rd January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Since $\Delta _{0}\gg P$, we ignore pairing energy and decide the electron arrangement mainly using $\Delta _{0}$.

For $[\mathrm{Co}(\mathrm{ox})_{3}]^{3-}$:

$\mathrm{Co}^{+3}$ has configuration $\mathrm{d}^{6}$.

In an octahedral field (given $\Delta _{0}\gg P$), all 6 electrons occupy $t_{2g}$ first, so the distribution is $\mathrm{t}_{2}\mathrm{g}^{2,2,2}\mathrm{eg}^{0,0}$.

Each electron in $t_{2g}$ gives CFSE of $(-0.4\Delta _{0})$, so

$\mathrm{CFSE}=6\times (-0.4\Delta _{0})=-2.4\Delta _{0}$

For $[\mathrm{Cr}(\mathrm{ox})_{3}]^{3-}$:

$\mathrm{Cr}^{+3}$ has configuration $\mathrm{d}^{3}$.

So the electrons occupy $t_{2g}$ as $\mathrm{t}_{2}\mathrm{g}^{1,1,1}\mathrm{eg}^{0,0}$.

Hence,

$\mathrm{CFSE}=3\times (-0.4\Delta _{0})=-1.2\Delta _{0}$

Now,

$\frac{(\mathrm{CFSE})_{\mathrm{Co}+3}}{(\mathrm{CFSE})_{\mathrm{Cr}+3}}=\frac{-2.4\Delta _{0}}{-1.2\Delta _{0}}=2$

So, $n=2$.

solution.body:
Starting from 1 mol $\mathrm{NH}{}_{3}$ with degree of dissociation $α$:


[IMG]

Total moles at equilibrium $=(1-α)+\dfrac{α}{2}+\dfrac{3α}{2}=1+α$, and $\Delta n_{g}=\dfrac{1}{2}+\dfrac{3}{2}-1=1$.

$K_{p}=\dfrac{\left (\dfrac{α}{2}\right )^{1/2}\left (\dfrac{3α}{2}\right )^{3/2}}{1-α}\times \dfrac{P}{1+α}=\dfrac{3\sqrt{3}\left (\dfrac{α}{2}\right )^{2}P}{1-α^{2}}$

With $P=\sqrt{3}$ atm and $K_{p}=9$ atm:

$9=\dfrac{9α^{2}}{4(1-α^{2})}\Rightarrow 4-4α^{2}=α^{2}\Rightarrow α^{2}=0.8$

$α=(0.8)^{1/2}=\left (\dfrac{1}{0.8}\right )^{-1/2}=\left (125\times 10^{-2}\right )^{-1/2}$

So $x=125$.

Hence, the answer is 125.

text:
For the thermal decomposition of reactant $\mathrm{AB}(\mathrm{g})$, the following plot is constructed.


[IMG]


The half life of the reaction is ' $x^{'}\min$.

$x=$ $____$ min. (Nearest integer)
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 23rd January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The graph between concentration $[\mathrm{AB}]$ and time $t$ is a straight line that decreases with time. This type of graph shows that the reaction is zero order in $[\mathrm{AB}]$.

For a zero-order reaction, the integrated rate law is:

$\begin{array}{l} [\mathrm{AB}]_{0}-[\mathrm{AB}]_{\mathrm{t}}=\mathrm{kt} \\ 𝟎\mathbf{.}𝟔 𝟎\mathbf{−}𝟎\mathbf{.}𝟓 𝟓\mathbf{=}𝐤(100) \\ \mathrm{k}=5\times 10^{-4} \\ \text{Half life}\left (\mathrm{t}_{1/2}\right )=\dfrac{[\mathrm{AB}]_{0}}{2\mathrm{k}} \\ =\dfrac{0.60}{2\times 5\times 10^{-4}} \\ =600\sec  \\ =10\min  \end{array}$

From the graph, the initial concentration is $[\mathrm{AB}]_{0}=0.60$ and after $100\text{s}$ the concentration is $0.55$. Substituting these values in the zero-order equation gives the rate constant $k=5\times 10^{-4}\text{mol L}^{-1}\text{s}^{-1}$.

For a zero-order reaction, the half-life is given by $t_{1/2}=\dfrac{[\mathrm{AB}]_{0}}{2k}$. Putting the values, we get $t_{1/2}=600\text{s}=10\text{\min }$. Therefore, $x=10\text{\min }$ (nearest integer).

text:
$x$ $\mathrm{mg}$ of pure HCl was used to make an aqueous solution. 25.0 mL of $0.1\mathrm{M}\mathrm{Ba}(\mathrm{OH})_{2}$ solution is used when the HCl solution was titrated against it. The numerical value of $x$ is $____$ $\times 10^{-1}$. (Nearest integer)

Given : Molar mass of HCl and $\mathrm{Ba}(\mathrm{OH})_{2}$ are 36.5 and $171.0\mathrm{g}\mathrm{mol}^{-1}$ respectively.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 23rd January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Balanced equation:

$\mathrm{Ba}(\mathrm{OH})_{2}+2\mathrm{HCl}\to \mathrm{BaCl}_{2}+2\mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{O}$

Moles of $\mathrm{Ba}(\mathrm{OH})_{2}$ used:

$n_{\mathrm{Ba}(\mathrm{OH})_{2}}=MV=0.1\times 25.0\times 10^{-3}=2.5\times 10^{-3}\text{mol}$

From the equation, $1$ mol $\mathrm{Ba}(\mathrm{OH})_{2}$ reacts with $2$ mol $\mathrm{HCl}$, so

$n_{\mathrm{HCl}}=2\times 2.5\times 10^{-3}=5.0\times 10^{-3}\text{mol}$

Mass of $\mathrm{HCl}$:

$m_{\mathrm{HCl}}=n\times M=5.0\times 10^{-3}\times 36.5=0.1825\text{g}$

$0.1825\text{g}=182.5\text{mg}$

So $x=182.5\text{mg}=1825\times 10^{-1}\text{mg}$.

Nearest integer $=1825$.
